name: LibreOffice
tagline: The full desktop office suite, no account needed
description: Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw and Base: a complete office suite that runs on your own computer. It opens and saves Microsoft formats and uses the OpenDocument standard natively.
backing: The Document Foundation, a German non-profit, with paid engineering from Collabora, allotropia and other ecosystem companies

maturity.rationale: Fifteen years of releases on a twice-yearly schedule (and a lineage going back to StarOffice), the default office suite on most Linux distributions, and deployed across public administrations such as Schleswig-Holstein.

strengths: Works entirely offline with no account and no subscription
Opens and saves .docx, .xlsx and .pptx as well as OpenDocument
Handles very large spreadsheets and legacy formats that web editors refuse
Can batch-convert whole folders of documents from the command line
weaknesses: No real-time co-editing: collaboration means passing files around, or pairing it with Collabora Online
Complex Word layouts, Excel pivot tables and PowerPoint animations can shift when files go back and forth
VBA macros run only partially; anything substantial needs rewriting

featureNotes.ms-format-fidelity: Good for everyday documents; test your most complex ones
featureNotes.browser-coediting: Collabora Online is the browser version of the same engine
